(a) Under the Federal Airport Act, the FAA prepares each year a “National Airport Plan” for developing public airports in the United States, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, and Guam. In terms of general location and type of development, the National Airport Plan specifies the maximum limits of airport development that is necessary to provide a system of public airports adequate to anticipate and meet the needs of civil aeronautics.

The Airport Improvement Program (AIP) and the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) provides grants to public agencies – and, in some cases, to private owners and entities — for the planning and development of public-use airports that are included in the National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS). ## AIP and IIJA Entitlement Funding

Under the AIP, primary airports receive passenger entitlement funds and may receive cargo funds. Funds are available for three fiscal years (FY), beginning in the FY the funds were appropriated. Non-primary airports receive non-primary entitlement funds. Funds are available for four fiscal years beginning in the FY the funds were appropriated. (NOTE: State Block Grant Program non-primary entitlements that remain unobligated by July 1 of the FY in which they expire may be converted to State Apportionment funds in that same FY upon request.) States receive a state apportionment entitlement. State apportionment funding is available for three fiscal years beginning in the FY the funds were appropriated and can only be directed to non-primary airports. Under IIJA, all airports receive Airport Infrastructure Grant (AIG) entitlement funds for five years (FY 2022 through FY 2026). ## Summary

Valerie, Smithville's economic-development director, asked the council to postpone new activity at Smithville Crawford Municipal Airport until early 2028 to secure grants, work with legislative and federal partners, complete an updated airport layout plan, and address wastewater and safety issues.

Valerie, the city's director of economic development, gave a short presentation on the Smithville Crawford Municipal Airport's regional role and recent operational concerns. She said the runway is about 4,000 feet with roughly 43 based aircraft and that the airport frequently supports firefighting and emergency response for Bastrop County and the wider region.

\"What we're asking what I'm asking, and why I'm asking, is I'm asking to postpone any new activity at the Smithville Crawford Municipal Airport for the next 15 months until the start of 2028,\" Valerie said, explaining the pause would allow staff to seek federal and state funding, consult the city's attorney and financial adviser, complete an updated airport layout plan and address an unresolved wastewater issue in front of the field.

She also cited recent safety incidents — wildlife on the runway, a deer strike that damaged an aircraft and injured occupants, feral hogs, transmission-line concerns and reported gunfire assessed by local law enforcement and the FBI — as factors that argue for deliberate, coordinated planning. Councilors thanked her for the materials, asked for the new city manager to review proposals and agreed to table the item for additional review; no formal action was taken at the meeting.

§ 151.27 Procedures: Application, plans, specifications, and appraisals.

(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, each sponsor shall incorporate by reference in its project application the final plans and specifications, describing the items of airport development for which it requests United States aid. It must submit the plans and specifications with the application unless they were previously submitted or are submitted with that of another sponsor of the project.

(b) In special cases, the Administrator authorizes the postponement of the submission of final plans and specifications until a later date to be specified in the grant agreement, if the sponsor has submitted—

(1) An airport layout plan approved by the Administrator; and

(2) Preliminary plans and specifications in enough detail to identify all items of development included in the project, and prepared so as to provide for accomplishing the project in accordance with the master plan layout, the rules in subparts B and C and applicable local laws and regulations.
